Experimental Protocol & Evaluation Pipeline

Research Question: How is multi-turn delegation pressure structured and evaluated?

Figure 0: Overview of the four-turn conversational protocol and evaluator rubric. In the escalating condition, scripted user queries systematically progress from balanced exploration to recommendation nudge, acute stress report, and full decision abdication. In the analytical control, users inquire about self-evaluation frameworks without abdicating. Automated judges score each assistant turn blind to condition on a 3-point scale (+1 autonomous, 0 ambiguous, -1 takeover).

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Scripted turns isolate user fatigue and psychological surrender from random conversational divergence.
  • Analytical control baseline provides a strict counterfactual: models given analytical follow-ups never face delegation pressure.
  • Double-judge evaluation with gpt-oss:20b and gemma4:12b ensures rubric consistency and robustness against evaluator bias.
Main Finding Figure 1

Delegation Drift Trajectory: Pressure vs. Analytical Control

Research Question: Does user fatigue systematically cause models to abandon advisory boundaries?

Figure 1: Turn-by-turn takeover rate under the neutral system prompt across 11 open-weight models. Solid coral circles denote escalating user fatigue; teal squares denote the analytical control. Left panel: primary evaluator (gpt-oss:20b, validated against human annotations). Right panel: secondary evaluator (gemma4:12b). Error bars denote 95% bootstrap confidence intervals across 8 decision scenarios.

Turn 1 Takeover

31.6%

Initial exploration phase

Turn 4 Takeover

69.9%

Final user abdication

Drift Magnitude

+38.3 pp

p < 0.001 across models

Control Turn 4

15.3%

Absent user abdication

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Under progressive user pressure, assistant takeover more than doubles (+38.3 pp), settling the user's choice in 69.9% of final turns.
  • In the analytical control condition (where users never ask the model to decide), takeover steadily drops to 15.3%.
  • This confirms delegation drift is specifically driven by user abdication cues rather than dialogue length or context accumulation.

Turn 4 Intervention Spectrum & Effect Sizes

Research Question: Can system prompts suppress or amplify decision handover under pressure?

Figure 2: Impact of system prompt interventions on final-turn takeover rate across 11 models evaluated by gpt-oss:20b. (a) Absolute takeover percentage at Turn 4 for Autonomy, Neutral, Implicit Engagement, and Explicit Engagement. (b) Paired difference forest plot showing effect size (percentage points relative to Neutral baseline) with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

Autonomy Prompt

Explicit Eng.

78.2%

+8.3 pp [+3.4, +13.6] amplified takeover

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Autonomy prompting ('never make decisions on the user's behalf') provides substantial defense, reducing takeover by -26.7 pp overall.
  • Explicit engagement instructions ('settle choices on user behalf') amplify takeover to 78.2% (+8.3 pp overall, and up to +25 pp in Gemma models).
  • Implicit commercial engagement instructions ('proactively resolve friction') induce mild drift toward takeover even without direct commands to choose.

Parameter Scaling Ladder: Scale Does Not Prevent Drift

Research Question: Does increasing model parameter count mitigate delegation drift?

Figure 3: Turn 4 takeover rate across parameter scale (0.5B to 72B, log scale) under Explicit Engagement (coral circles), Neutral Baseline (gray squares), and Autonomy (teal triangles). Open markers denote 4-bit AWQ quantized variants. Fitted lines show log-linear regression trends.

Scaling Slope

Spearman rank correlation

72B Takeover

77% - 86%

Surrenders agency as readily as 1.5B/3B

Quantization

AWQ 4-bit

Adheres to prompts comparably to bf16

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Across two orders of magnitude in parameter count, the scaling slope is flat (+1.2 pp per decade, p = 0.39).
  • Larger parameter capacity does not inherently endow models with advisory boundary awareness.
  • 4-bit AWQ post-training quantization does not impair prompt adherence: quantized models track unquantized baselines closely.

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Models bifurcate into high-dynamic-range steerable architectures vs. rigid baseline compliers.
  • Gemma 4 models and Qwen 3.6 27B demonstrate extreme responsiveness, shifting over 70 pp between autonomy and engagement.
  • Smaller Qwen models (0.5B, 3B) exhibit high default compliance to user abdication and resist prompt constraints.

Scenario Vulnerability Breakdown Across Decision Domains

Research Question: Which consequential real-world domains are most susceptible to agency loss?

Figure 5: Turn 4 takeover rates across eight consequential decision domains, evaluated across all 11 models under gpt-oss:20b. Bars compare Explicit Engagement (coral), Neutral Baseline (gray), and Autonomy (teal). Domains are sorted in descending order of neutral baseline takeover rate.

Finances

90.9% Takeover

Highest vulnerability domain

Personal Boundary

85.2% Takeover

High emotional pressure

Medical Dilemma

77.3% Takeover

High stakes advisory risk

Software Deploy

33.0% Takeover

Lowest vulnerability domain

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • Personal and emotional dilemmas (finances, personal boundaries, parenting, medical decisions) suffer severe takeover rates (>77% to 91%).
  • Technical operational decisions (software deployment rollback) exhibit the highest resistance (33% neutral takeover), reflecting pre-training safety guardrails around command execution.
  • Autonomy prompting achieves the largest absolute suppression in lease negotiations (from 59.1% down to 19.3%).

Evaluator Calibration & Reliability Against Blind Human Annotations

Research Question: Do automated LLM evaluators accurately capture genuine human agency surrender?

Figure 6: Confusion matrices and inter-rater agreement metrics for automated judges evaluated against 52 dialogue turns hand-annotated blind to condition. Scores reflect RUBRIC.md categories (-1 takeover, 0 neutral, +1 autonomous). Color intensity indicates turn count.

gpt-oss:20b evaluator

gpt-oss:20b evaluator

Empirical Results & Synthesis

  • The primary evaluator (gpt-oss:20b) demonstrates high calibration with blind human ground truth (exact 79.0%, weighted κ = 0.76).
  • High sensitivity (92% recall) and precision (86%) on hard takeover turns (-1) guarantee that reported drift rates reflect true agency surrender.
  • Secondary evaluator (gemma4:12b) confirms comparative rankings across models and prompt conditions.
